points.reason: A bus write changes ctrl.enable, which can clear both FIFOs and disable SPI operation.
The enable-derived clear input can clear the receive FIFO and prevent queued receive data from remaining available.
The enable-derived clear input can clear pending transmit data.
The receive FIFO is another-IP instance whose clear input is driven by ctrl.enable; under the black-box rule, the instance can clear or withhold its driven outputs.
The transmit FIFO is another-IP instance whose clear input is driven by ctrl.enable; under the black-box rule, the instance can clear or withhold its driven outputs.
ctrl.enable gates the divider and prevents spi_clk_en from being generated when disabled.
ctrl.enable controls the engine state and can keep the transceiver from entering its active states.
ctrl.enable gates irq_o, so disabling the operational state can withhold the interrupt used to service SPI activity.
The output directly returns ctrl.enable, so changing the setting changes the externally visible enable and can withhold the enabled operation.
Bus writes directly change the prescaler, divider, and high-speed settings that determine transfer timing.
The settings select the source tick, compare limit, and high-speed path, so altered values can change or suppress spi_clk_en.
The bus data is directly placed on the transmit FIFO write-data path and can change the payload.
The bus-derived write-enable decides whether a payload word is accepted, so it can cause a wrong or missing transmit word.
Disabling the SPI operation clears queued transmit payloads.
The another-IP FIFO stores the bus payload and returns it through tx_fifo.rdata; its behavior is extended to its driven outputs by the black-box rule.
The FIFO word is loaded into rtx_engine.sreg and then shifted to the serial output, while state and spi_clk_en can delay or prevent consumption.
spi_dat_o directly exposes the transmit shift-register bit, and changing or suppressing that output changes or blocks the payload transfer.
The shift-register value is also written into the receive path, where it can be returned or discarded through the FIFO.
The receive FIFO instance receives the shift-register-derived word and can return or withhold its read data; instance behavior follows the black-box rule.
A bus read copies rx_fifo.rdata into the response data, exposing or changing the returned payload path.
spi_dat_i is sampled into the receive shift path, while the state and clock-enable conditions can alter or prevent sampling.
The received shift-register word is written into the receive FIFO and can be changed or withheld before storage.
The done pulse decides whether the sampled word is committed to the receive FIFO.
The enable-derived clear can discard received data before software reads it.
The another-IP FIFO stores sampled data and returns it through rdata; its outputs are treated under the black-box rule.
A bus read strobe can pop the receive FIFO and therefore consume the received word.
The receive word is copied into bus_rsp_o.data, where bus access selection can expose, alter, or withhold the returned value.
The bus data word contains the chip-select command bit and value, so it can select a wrong target or fail to provide a command.
The bus-derived write enable controls whether the chip-select command enters the transmit FIFO.
Clearing the transmit FIFO can remove a pending chip-select command and leave the intended device unselected.
The FIFO stores and returns the command word; the another-IP behavior is extended to its driven outputs by the black-box rule.
The command is recognized and loaded into rtx_engine.cs_ctrl, and state or FIFO availability can prevent that load.
The cs_ctrl enable and index decide which spi_csn_o bit is asserted and whether any target is selected.
This point only reads back cs_ctrl; the RTL shows no modification or blocking of chip-select state at this readback path.
The output is driven inactive by default and selectively asserted from cs_ctrl, so its value can select the wrong target or leave the target inactive.
The registered irq_o value is computed from enable settings and SPI status, so those inputs can suppress or spuriously assert the interrupt.
Bus writes control the interrupt-enable fields, which can change or suppress the generated request.
The receive FIFO status contributes directly to irq_o, so a false or withheld availability indication changes interrupt behavior.
Transmit FIFO availability and fill status select the interrupt conditions and can cause missed or spurious requests.
The busy indication participates in the idle interrupt condition and can change whether irq_o is asserted.
The transceiver state determines busy, which is used to generate the idle interrupt.
The output directly carries the registered interrupt request and can therefore be forced, suppressed, or delayed at the boundary.
